survivors.coaching/postRaceRecoveryCurve.test.ts :: EQUIVALENT, proved by reading: `raceWeekN >= plan.weeks.length` is an early return, and when it is skipped the very next guard `windowEnd < raceWeekN + 1` evaluates to the identical condition (with no following race, windowEnd IS plan.weeks.length). Both paths return null for the same inputs. The first guard is a cheap early exit, not a distinct rule; nothing a test can observe distinguishes them.

EQUIVALENT, proved by the caller contract: idx comes from `findIndex((w, i) => i + 1 > raceWeekN && ...)`, so a hit at index 0 would need raceWeekN < 1. raceWeekN is 1-indexed and every caller passes >= 1, so idx is never 0 when found and `>= 0` and `> 0` cannot differ. Would stop being equivalent if a caller ever passed 0 — which would be its own defect.
survivors.coaching/reshapeMagnitude.test.ts :: fli: EQUIVALENT: `kind === 'modified' || (before && after)` only widens entry to the branch for kinds that reach L82 at all, and replaced/added/removed all return 'high' at L79 first. The only other kind is 'unchanged', which computeSessionDiff builds with label, distance AND duration equal — so the distance comparison inside yields 0% and returns the same 'low'.

EQUIVALENT, proved at the producer: computeSessionDiff (lib/coaching/diff/sessionDiff.ts:101) constructs kind 'modified' only as `{ before: bb, after: aa }` with both non-null. `before && after` is therefore always true for a 'modified' entry, and `before || after` is too.
survivors.plan/fitnessThresholds.test.ts :: pertur: EQUIVALENT: mutates FITNESS_RANK.experienced from 2 to 3. The map's absolute values are arbitrary — every consumer uses it for ORDERING only (`FITNESS_RANK[byVdot] < FITNESS_RANK[byVolume]` in assessFitness), and the test asserts the ordering, which still holds. Fixing this would mean asserting a number nothing depends on.

unproven_reasons.coaching/dayBoundary.test.ts: dayBoundary.ts is 48 lines with ZERO comparison operators and no code-level numeric literal — the battery has nothing to flip. Its logic is date arithmetic via Date methods. Widening the battery to mutate method calls (getTime/setHours) is the way to reach it; until then this is the harness's limit, not the test's.
unproven_reasons.coaching/readinessBaseline.test.ts: Imported symbols resolve to threshold LOOKUPS against lib/coaching/constants.ts rather than comparisons inside readinessBaseline.ts itself, so the in-scope spans contain no mutable operator. Reaching it means mutating the CONSTANTS module, which would change behaviour for every test at once and produce unreadable attribution.
unproven_reasons.coaching/recalibrationPrompt.test.ts: Same shape: the scheduling decision is date comparison plus a config lookup, with no operator inside the imported declarations. The test's own assertions (fires only on a completed recalibration-week time trial, never on a non-TT day) are its liveness evidence for now.
